subject: Civil Engineering
title: How Suspension Bridges Work
description: Learn How Suspension Bridges Work in one minute.

hook.text: The Golden Gate's twin cables hold 80,000 miles of wire. The deck hangs from them.

buildup.text: Main cables drape between towers. Vertical hangers transfer the deck's weight up.

discovery.text: Cables work in pure tension — the most efficient way to carry load over distance.

twist.text: The cables pull inward on the towers, which must resist as giant compression columns.

climax.text: Anchorages at each end pull the cables into massive concrete blocks or bedrock.

punchline.text: Hang the road from cables and you can cross almost anything.

quiz.question: What structural role do the towers play in a suspension bridge?
options: They carry the deck directly on beams
They resist the inward pull of the cables as compression columns
They anchor the cables into the ground at each end

details.summary: Suspension bridges hang the roadway deck from vertical cables attached to massive main cables that drape between tall towers and are anchored at each end. The main cables transfer the deck's weight into tension, which the cables carry to the towers and anchorages as compression and pull forces.
details.whyItMatters: Suspension bridges achieve the longest spans of any bridge type because cables in pure tension are the most efficient structural elements. Every record-breaking bridge span uses suspension design.
takeaways: Main cables carry the entire deck load in pure tension
Towers transfer cable forces to foundations as vertical compression
Anchorages resist the enormous horizontal pull of the main cables

faq.question: Why can suspension bridges span longer distances than any other type?
faq.answer: Cables in pure tension use material at its maximum efficiency since every fiber carries load. The parabolic cable shape naturally distributes weight evenly. Towers need only resist vertical compression, not bending. This combination allows spans exceeding 2,000 meters.

faq.question: What keeps a suspension bridge from swaying dangerously in wind?
faq.answer: Modern suspension bridges use aerodynamic deck shapes tested in wind tunnels, stiffening trusses or box girders beneath the deck, and tuned mass dampers to absorb energy. These features prevent the resonance that destroyed the original Tacoma Narrows Bridge in 1940.
